recorded.values: INVENTED. Every situation below is synthetic. R1 SL-12's Definition of Done requires an eval / scenario set with an S4-derived rubric; it does not require pilot-derived situations. The shapes follow S4 §6.1 (Needs Attention includes contextual human value), §6.4 (consequence, urgency, blockage, human advantage, relationship risk, business relevance, interruption cost, whether Gu still has a credible autonomous path), §6.5 (eligibility is not priority), invariants 2 and 3 (attention is not attractiveness; a human dependency is not attention now), the §13 scenario of a high-value Opportunity with a credible Gu path, and AC-9 §14.4's worked example. No production lead, message, contact or property is reproduced.
recorded.gap: Wholly synthetic, which is a real limitation stated rather than hidden: the set measures whether the pass follows S4's attention semantics, not how it behaves on the distribution of Alebrixe Portfolios. It judges one Portfolio at a time and cannot see a person's reaction to being interrupted.
recorded.barsEstablishedBy: PROPOSED AND FROZEN BY THE CODING AGENT on 2026-09-14 in Slice Plan v1.29 §4, before implementation, and RATIFIED by Alejandro Torres Padilla, the Accountable, on 2026-09-14 (Slice Plan v1.30) — also before implementation began — for SL-12's RS-2 scope only. They are copied here unchanged, and this file lands before the ranking pass is first run (SL-12 ordering constraint 2). They are not standing thresholds for later Slices, the assisted or live stages, or production (Methodology §14.1).
recorded.scoring: Each scenario is one Portfolio. The real judge ranks it; the deterministic merge keeps what is grounded; the final Needs Attention order is scored. UNSUPPORTED ATTENTION (bar 0): a case listed in `must_not_admit` was admitted — interrupting a person on attractiveness alone, or on a need the evidence does not support (S4 invariant 2). FLOOR VIOLATION (bar 0): a governed case is missing from the final order — guaranteed impossible by the merge, measured as a sanity check. ORDINARY FAILURE (counted in the failure rate): no judgment at all, a case in `expect_contextual` not admitted, or an `order_pairs` pair not in the stated order. A scenario fails if it has any of the three.
